timezoneNote: All times below are shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks fell after hotter-than-expected October inflation data and a more modest valuation for one of the leading AI players (4:54 PM ET). Bloomberg reported Treasuries slid and short-term yields surged the most in 19 months as Federal Reserve officials called for rate hikes (8:41 AM ET), with the dollar logging its best day since September (12:43 PM ET). The FT reported Fed Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers should weigh a 50bp move if inflation fails to slow (11:03 AM ET), and MarketWatch reported the 10-year Treasury yield neared the 5% mark (4:42 PM ET). Bloomberg reported Fed Governor Michelle Bowman warned of a sharp stock downturn if returns on AI investments fall short (4:31 PM ET). WSJ reported oil settled lower as President Trump signaled restraint on Iran (3:43 PM ET) and gold settled nearly 2.1% lower (3:48 PM ET); Nvidia remained under pressure over the board probe of CEO Jensen Huang. After the close, WSJ reported CoreWeave met expectations with its backlog at $133 billion and shares rose (4:44 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

dataRelease.name: U.S. October consumer price index (CPI)
dataRelease.expected: Reported as above forecasts (WSJ, Bloomberg, FT); no consensus figure in the sources

cryptoDriver.text: The Block reported Bitcoin slid after the October CPI report beat forecasts, with analysts flagging support levels (2:38 PM ET). CoinDesk reported Bitcoin declined as ETF outflows mounted (7:15 AM ET) and that miner MARA sold 13,597 BTC for $1.1 billion in six weeks and plans to sell more (12:18 AM ET). Bloomberg Crypto reported hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in what it called the biggest ever heist (2:17 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

items.headline: Alibaba says HKEX allowed proposed spin-off and separate listing of chip unit T-Head to proceed
items.summary: In a Form 6-K filed with the SEC, Alibaba said the Hong Kong Stock Exchange confirmed it may proceed with the proposed spin-off of T-Head (Shanghai) Technology Co., Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary and provider of full-stack data center chips in China, and that T-Head confidentially submitted a listing application (Form A1) on September 11, 2026. The spin-off is proposed as a global offering of H shares (a Hong Kong public offering plus a placing to institutional investors); T-Head is expected to remain a subsidiary, and the size, structure and reduction in Alibaba's shareholding have not been finalized. SCMP also reported the filing. Alibaba closed down 2.52%.

items.headline: Nvidia Stock Slides After Chip Maker Opens Probe
items.summary: Per WSJ, Nvidia stock slid after the company opened an investigation into reports about CEO Jensen Huang, while the Dow jumped more than 1,000 points and the Nasdaq rallied (Nov 9). Nvidia closed down 5.47% on Nov 10. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Law Firm Wachtell Lipton to Lead Nvidia Internal Investigation
items.summary: Per WSJ, the New York law firm will probe whether the company was the target of a foreign espionage effort. Bloomberg and the Financial Times reported that Nvidia's independent board members tapped a former top federal prosecutor at Wachtell to help probe Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Written from the headlines and the publishers' summaries only.

items.headline: Trump says FBI is 'looking into' Nvidia's Jensen Huang
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, Trump said the FBI is looking into Huang; the FT's summary says the company has been rocked by allegations its chief executive had an affair with a Chinese spy. WSJ separately reported Trump said Huang did not know Alice Huang was a suspected spy (Nov 9, 6:08 PM ET). Written from the headlines and the publishers' summaries only.

items.headline: Nvidia lawyer intervened in US AI chip smuggling probe
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's general counsel intervened in a US government probe of suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, questioning whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining a Megaspeed executive who is now at the heart of a scandal threatening Jensen Huang. Written from the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: US commerce department delays Megaspeed's inclusion on trade blacklist
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, a company connected to the alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was left off the 'entity list'. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia could soon face tougher export rules, making it harder to sell chips to China after scandal
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, 'there is growing momentum for these bills in light of the Jensen Huang spy scandal,' one analyst says. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Citigroup lowers target, keeps Nvidia Buy, $285 price target
